parts.mapping: H/h determine hooked/straight pods and S/s speckled/plain petals in a fictional complete-dominance model. Parents are HhSS × hhSs; the sample is120 offspring. Ordinary segregation, independent assortment, random fertilisation, reliable expression and no phenotype-dependent loss are explicit.
parts.limits: Trait rules, genotypes and sample size are authored teaching parameters, not observations or verified real-plant trait claims.

parts.mapping: HS/hS and hS/hs are each parent’s two distinct gametes. The 2×2 table yields HhSS, HhSs, hhSS and hhSs with probability one quarter each.
parts.limits: Neither parent is heterozygous at both loci. This demonstrates contribution accounting and grouping; it does not prove two-locus independence. The stated independence assumption is stronger than necessary for this particular cross, but is not false.

parts.mapping: Four genotype classes in a1:1:1:1 ratio group into hooked/speckled and straight/speckled with probability one half each. Exact HhSS has probability one quarter; hooked/speckled has probability one half. No genotype is ss.

parts.part: Derived classic ratio and its scope
parts.mapping: For two double heterozygotes, each complete-dominance locus gives3:1. Under independent assortment the relative weights are3×3,3×1,1×3 and1×1, totaling16 gamete pairings and giving9:3:3:1. The text names all four phenotype categories and limits the ratio to the stated parents and assumptions.
parts.limits: This essential derivation structurally supports the protected3/16 class. It is not represented as a new solved response to the exact AaBb × AaBb / P(aaB_) required prompt.

parts.mapping: Knowing each allele occurs in half the gametes does not establish independent combinations. Add mutually exclusive categories to find marginal totals and compare the proposed product with the stipulated joint value.
